annotations.title: Make, rename, order and remove deduction types, and say what each counts as and pays into

description: Everything the deduction types screen does, for **several types in one call**: **make** a type (its name, what the paycheck calls it, its kind), **rename** one, change its kind, **remove** one, put the list in **order**, and say what each type **counts as** (out of net, saving — the two flags every paycheck figure turns on) and what it **pays into** — a fund or a goal for a saving line, a debt (a payroll loan) for a loan repayment. **This link is how a fund finds its paycheck lines**: a pension line is a deposit into a fund only because its type names the fund, and `funds` checks those deposits against the fund’s own report. A new type starts as its kind’s guess, and a kind change carries the flags along while they are still the guess; one that differs is shown as set by hand, and `guess` puts it back. One destination per type — naming one clears the others, and `pays_into: null` links nothing. Refused by name: a target of the wrong kind (a fund or a goal takes a line that counts as saving, a debt a loan repayment), a name another type has, and removing a built-in type, a type a stored paycheck line names, or one another row links to. Types and their ids are listed by `paychecks`; funds by `funds`, goals by `savings`, debts by `debts`. **Dry-runs by default**; the batch applies whole or not at all, and the document is copied to a timestamped .bak first.

commit.description: Default false. False previews; true writes.

order.description: Types by id or by name — the names they will have after this call, new ones included. These come first in the list, in this order, and the rest follow as they are.

path.description: Absolute path to a .emd file on this machine.

types.description: One entry per deduction type, up to 60 in a call. With `type` it changes or removes that type; without it, it makes a new one, which needs `name` and `kind`.

counts_as.description: What its amounts count as: out_of_net_saving (a pension, a study fund), out_of_net (a tax, a repayment), saving (employer money that never touches net — severance), not_cash (a benefit in kind), or guess — what its kind says. Leave it out to keep it (a new type takes its kind’s guess).

kind.description: What kind of line it is. Needed for a new type; on an existing one it changes the kind.

name.description: The new type’s name, or the new name of the type in `type`.

on_the_slip.description: What the paycheck calls it, as printed; null clears it. Leave it out to keep it.

pays_into.description: A fund, a goal or a debt, by id or by name; null to link nothing. Leave it out to keep the link.

pays_into_kind.description: Only when the name is both a fund and a goal, say: which one is meant.

remove.description: True removes the type in `type`, and the entry takes nothing else.

type.description: An existing deduction type, by id (`ded:pension`), by name, or by what the paycheck calls it. Leave it out to make a new type.

name: set_deduction_types
